messages:
ivy: FYI onboarding peregrine-11b-int4 tonight. repro shows transient OOMs during mixed warmup (short chats + one very long generation ~3k tokens) and a small METEOR drop on long-context summarization. jotting notes + a conservative canary plan. :wave:

noel: can you paste the runner snippet + quick repro steps?

ivy: runner (trimmed):
```
model: peregrine-11b-int4
batch_target: auto
max_new_tokens: 200
kv_prefetch: eager
kv_prefetch_window: 0
slot_compactor_interval: 60s
soft_reserve: 0.10
dynamic_kv_mode: off
```
repro: cold hosts, ramp 10 concurrent chat sessions (~120 tokens), then 1 long summarize (~3000 tokens). node hits low free_slots -> transient OOM; compactor reclaims ~600MiB and host recovers.

priya: allocator excerpt? even a couple lines.

ivy: pasted allocator lines:
```
[2026-03-25T11:12:01Z] gpu_alloc fail 1.14GiB
[2026-03-25T11:12:02Z] kv_live=4.05GiB
[2026-03-25T11:12:03Z] free_slots_frac=0.025
[2026-03-25T11:12:06Z] compactor reclaimed=610MiB
```

zack: int4 reduces model weights but KV still grows with seq_len. couple of mitigations we've not tried together: 1) sliding-window prefetch (limit to recent tokens) + token-preserving trimming (drop oldest KV entries but keep a lightweight residue to preserve positional continuity), 2) dynamic KV encoding switch: allocate fp16-KV proactively for predicted long gens to avoid conversion spikes.

noel: curious about METEOR regression. where is it concentrated?

ivy: METEOR drop ~0.7 absolute on summaries >900 tokens. short summaries no significant delta. hypothesis: quantized KV accumulation + stale positional residue causing drift in long decodes. need per-layer activation-error and token-logprob diffs.

priya: propose a conservative canary that tries the least-invasive levers first:
- set model default max_new_tokens -> 64 for peregrine-11b-int4 (rollbackable)
- enable kv_prefetch_window = 256 (sliding-window)
- enable token_preserve_trim = true (trim oldest KV but keep 1 token-residue per block)
- enable dynamic_kv_mode = proactive (allocate fp16-KV if predicted_gen_len > 512)
- batch_pacing_ms = 40 on canary hosts
- reduce slot_compactor_interval = 30s for canary hosts
- warmup_soft_reserve = 0.14 only for hosts tagged warmup
- run the summarization eval harness (160 long examples) + perf sweep (p50/p95 token lat)

ivy: i'll open PR and start a 4% dedicated canary. aim: 2k requests or 6 hours. tagging long-gen requests for trace sampling.

zack: evaluation targets: p95 token latency < 160ms, memory cushion >= 512MiB post-warmup, METEOR >= float_baseline - 0.8. if METEOR delta > 0.8 -> revert quant rollout and collect per-layer symmetric/asymmetric quant histograms.

noel: two operational notes: 1) proactive fp16-KV allocation ups peak mem slightly but avoids conversion allocation spikes mid-gen; 2) token_preserve_trim tries to avoid positional discontinuities by keeping a small residue which in practice reduced quality regressions in previous tests.

priya: sample curl to hit canary (replace TOKEN):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://dedicated-canary.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
  -H \"Model: peregrine-11b-int4\" \\
  -d '{\"input\":\"<long summarize prompt>\",\"max_new_tokens\":64}'
```
infra-bot: :gear: canary policy applied  peregrine-11b-int4 -> 4% Dedicated canary. ChangeSet: infra/2026-peregrine-canary-01. PR: #2401 opened by ivy.

zack: i'll schedule a perf-snapshot after ~1k requests to capture slab maps and per-layer activation diffs. if we see error concentrated in specific layers we can try targeted per-layer fp16-KV mapping next.

ivy: remote QA plan: run 160 long-document summaries + 240 short chats; capture per-token logprob diffs and per-layer L2 error heatmaps. will post results back here.

noel: alerting rules to wire: memory_cushion < 256MiB -> immediate rollback; METEOR delta > 0.8 -> pause rollout and collect artifacts; p95 token latency > 220ms -> scale down canary.

deploy-bot: :robot_face: canary updated  peregrine-11b-int4 defaults -> 4% Dedicated canary. PR #2401 created.

ivy: thanks  i'll update this thread with the eval outputs and any followups (per-layer snapshots, kernel-sched tweak if needed). :mag:
